fuentes.fuente: WRB and USDA soil catalog; 32 WRB reference soil groups (30 with a summary sheet from Driessen et al. 2001, Lecture Notes on the Major Soils of the World, FAO World Soil Resources Reports 94; Technosols and Stagnosols without one), 12 USDA Soil Taxonomy orders (formative element from Moorberg and Crouse 2017; definition and fertility from University of Idaho and Lancaster University [P]), 20 great-group prefixes and formative elements (SSSA, Glossary of Soil Science Terms, Table A2; «arg» from Moorberg and Crouse 2017, Table 4.3) and the soils of the municipality of Delicias (Municipal Development Plan 2024–2027, citing INEGI 2016); all read on Nov 14, 2026, each block with its link; landscape context, it does not say which nutrients a field has

fuentes.fuente: Project assumptions (datos/supuestos.json): each with value, label and source; those marked assumption [S] have no local source. Includes ea_goteo = 0.90 and ea_superficial_referencia = 0.60, indicative values from FAO, Irrigation Water Management Training Manual No. 4 (1989), Annex I, Table 8 (not measured in DR-005); lamina_local_cm, irrigation depths recommended by INIFAP and applied in DR-005 in 2009–2016 (Villalobos-Cano et al. 2024, DOI 10.3390/su16051851), as a reference; cobertura_ndvi_relacion and nogal_referencia (a reference that the calculation does not use); suelo_margen_ph (0.5, assumption [S]) and suelo_coincidencia_textura (0.47, own analysis)

fuentes.fuente: OpenLandMap, USDA soil great groups (Predicted USDA soil great groups at 250 m, Hengl and Nauman 2018, v01, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1476844, CC-BY-SA 4.0), Earth Engine OpenLandMap/SOL/SOL_GRTGROUP_USDA-SOILTAX_C/v01, band grtgroup; great group of the field = most frequent class among the cells whose center falls inside (or the nearest cell, at 250 m or less); order from the formative element of the name (Moorberg and Crouse 2017) and the formative elements present (SSSA, Table A2); two pilot areas; prediction of a global model, not a soil survey
